caveats: Evidence base completed on 2026-09-06: the blog crosswalk ROAT-2026-0317 is no longer cited as core evidence; every row rests on a primary legal or technical source (Vienna Convention 1968 and Art. 34 bis, SAE J3016/J3018, Swedish Ordinance 2017:309 and TSFS 2021:4, NTC Australia ADSE policy paper, Japan Act No. 32 of 2022, California Veh. Code § 38750, Ontario O. Reg. 161/25 and the ACMV Program Conditions).

Remote intervention is coded as intervention from outside the vehicle. In-vehicle commands and takeovers (RC-012, RC-020, RC-022) are therefore 'No' with a qualifier; the same information remains in the Fallback and Dispatch columns.

RC-009: AFGBV § 14(3) with Annex 1 no. 4 requires the technical supervision person to take over manually after a defect-triggered minimal-risk manoeuvre and allows near-field remote control (6 m, walking speed); the cell records this boundary case, not remote driving in the ordinary sense.
RC-014: 'Arranged if remote takeover' rests on parliamentary print 1329 read with the proposed § 5(6) of Act No. 8/2009 Coll.; confirm the wording at the next revision of the print.
RC-021 (remote prototype fallback test driver): SAE J3018_202012 names the role but defers its guidance to a future iteration — the cell records the definition, not operational requirements.
RC-025 (ADS lifecycle safety entity) rests on a consultation policy paper; the Australian Automated Vehicle Safety Law is not yet enacted.
55 first-pass cells affirm a function for which the second coder found no passage in the listed sources; they stand on the first coder's reading and are queued for pinpointing at the next revision.
Coding date per row is the 'Last checked' column in the Hub.
